```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(REPS)
```

## Introduction

Sales price appraisal ratio (SPAR) indices measure price development using
transaction prices and appraisal values. `calculate_spar_index()` supports
three methods: `"arithmetic"`, `"geometric"`, and `"unweighted"`.

## Required data

Supply a data frame with one row per property transaction. Each row should
match the transaction price to an appraisal value for the same property,
and identify when the sale took place. Prices and appraisals should use the
same currency and units; supply their original values without taking logs.
SPAR does not require explanatory variables such as floor area or neighbourhood,
or repeated sales of the same property.

The example uses these five columns; your own column names can differ:

| Column | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `period` | Transaction month, for example `201301` for January 2013. |
| `appraisal_year` | Valuation vintage to which the appraisal value refers. |
| `price` | Numeric transaction price. |
| `property_type` | Category used here to calculate separate housing series. |
| `appraisal_value` | Numeric appraisal value for the transacted property. |

Use `grouping_variables` to identify short-term groups with the same appraisal
vintage and any categories you want to keep separate. Property type is an
optional way to split the data, rather than a required SPAR characteristic.
In this example, grouping by appraisal year and property type creates one
short-term index for each combination.

Observed prices and appraisal values must be positive and finite. Missing
values are omitted during aggregation, but each period/group needs enough
observed values for the selected method. Period and group identifiers must
not be missing or blank. Each group needs its reference period, January by
default; groups without a matching reference are warned about and omitted.

## Example data

```{r example-data}
data("arithmetic_data")
head(arithmetic_data)
```

Column arguments below are supplied as strings.

## Calculate a SPAR index

Group by appraisal year and property type to calculate separate short-term
indices. The default reference period is January, with an index level of 100.

```{r single-method}
spar_arithmetic <- calculate_spar_index(
  dataset = arithmetic_data,
  method = "arithmetic",
  period_variable = "period",
  dependent_variable = "price",
  appraisal_variable = "appraisal_value",
  grouping_variables = c("appraisal_year", "property_type")
)
head(spar_arithmetic)
```

## Multiple methods

Supply a method vector to receive a named list of results.

```{r multiple-methods}
spar <- calculate_spar_index(
  dataset = arithmetic_data,
  method = c("arithmetic", "geometric", "unweighted"),
  period_variable = "period",
  dependent_variable = "price",
  appraisal_variable = "appraisal_value",
  grouping_variables = c("appraisal_year", "property_type")
)
names(spar)
```

## Chained SPAR

Chained SPAR uses monthly YYYYMM periods with January as the reference period.
Here, `property_type` identifies the independent series to chain across
appraisal years. Each short-term group must cover a single calendar year
and start in January, with only one appraisal vintage per month within each
independent series.

```{r chained-spar}
spar_chained <- calculate_spar_index(
  dataset = arithmetic_data,
  method = c("arithmetic", "geometric", "unweighted"),
  period_variable = "period",
  dependent_variable = "price",
  appraisal_variable = "appraisal_value",
  grouping_variables = c("appraisal_year", "property_type"),
  chained = TRUE,
  index_type_variable = "property_type"
)
```

## Index contribution

For a single method, add `index_contribution = TRUE` to inspect each
observation's influence on the index level and period-on-period change.
The latest period is analyzed by default; use `index_contribution_period`
to choose another period or `unit_variable` to exclude units together.

```{r index-contribution}
result <- calculate_spar_index(
  dataset = arithmetic_data,
  method = "arithmetic",
  period_variable = "period",
  dependent_variable = "price",
  appraisal_variable = "appraisal_value",
  grouping_variables = c("appraisal_year", "property_type"),
  index_contribution = TRUE
)
head(result$Index)
head(result$Index_contribution)
```

## Bootstrap margins

Add `margins = TRUE` for bootstrap margins around the original index, with
`confidence_level = 0.95` and `bootstrap_replicates = 999` by default.
`bootstrap_strata = NULL` samples the full dataset; use column names such as
`c("period", "appraisal_year", "property_type")` to retain those group sizes.
Call `set.seed()` beforehand for reproducible results.

## Plotting

Filter to one property type before comparing the three chained methods.

```{r plotting, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
apartments <- lapply(spar_chained, function(x) {
  x[x$property_type == "Apartment", ]
})
plot_price_index(apartments, title = "SPAR indices: apartments")
```

## Summary

Use one method for a data frame or several for a named list. Add chaining to
link appraisal years, and enable index contribution when analyzing a single
method's observations.
